scopeNote: These fixtures verify minute-level Gregorian local wall-clock resolution against the runtime IANA timezone database. They classify repeated and skipped local minutes; they do not invent a disambiguation choice for the user.

evidence.finding: NIST states that U.S. daylight saving time begins at 02:00 local on the second Sunday in March by skipping forward to 03:00, and ends at 02:00 local on the first Sunday in November by moving back to 01:00 so that hour repeats.

MDN documents that Intl.DateTimeFormat accepts IANA timezone identifiers such as America/New_York and provides an explicit h23 hour cycle, allowing deterministic formatting independent of the host machine local timezone.

MDN documents formatToParts as a widely available way to retrieve year, month, day, hour and minute tokens separately, which lets the resolver compare a candidate instant to the exact requested local wall-clock minute without locale-string parsing.
